newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Masood, Dostum meet, Rabbani government recognised.
newsitem.headline: Masood, Dostum meet, Rabbani government recognised.

text.p: Uzbek commander Adbul Rashid Dostum recognised the ousted Rabbani goverment of Afghanistan on Monday but stopped short of an alliance with its forces around Kabul, a Dostum spokesman said.

"We recognised Mr. Rabbani's government and we set up a commission today to consider the proper roles and responsibilities of the (Dostum forces) in the government as well as those of other parties," General Mohamed Youssef, a Dostum spokesman, told reporters after the meeting.

Ousted Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani, former army chief Ahmad Shah Masood, Dostum and other key players who oppose the Taleban movement in Afghanistan met for more than five hours at the top of the Salang pass north of Kabul in an attempt to coordinate strategy against their foes.

The meeting also managed to appoint an executive committee for the ad hoc Council for the Defence of Afghanistan, which included Dostum, Masood and Karim Khalili, head of the Shia Moslem Hezb-i-Wahadat.
The Islamic Taleban, who took over the capital on September 27, have suffered serious military reverses in the past few days, losing key towns to Masood.

A Masood spokesman said that his forces had captured all but the very tip of the Bagram airbase in fighting on Monday and were ensconced at various points in and around the periphery of the Afghan capital.
